RDZ Package Review — Post Phase 0B

Source: review.md

Review date: 2026-08-08 Reviewed at: branch feature/init, working tree as of the Phase 0B completion checkpoint recorded in current-state.md.

Scope and verification

This review covers the R public API, the Rust container/codec/IO modules, the Phase 0B wire contract, the test suites, and source packaging.

Check Command Result
Pure Rust tests cargo test --manifest-path src/rust/Cargo.toml 9/9 pass
R integration tests Rscript -e 'testthat::test_local(reporter = "summary")' all pass, 0 failures (benchmark-tools, correctness, public-api)
Source build R CMD build . succeeds, but see finding 1

Findings 1 and 2 were reproduced empirically; the rest were established by reading the sources and the format contract. Finding 3 was raised, tested, and withdrawn — see below.

Reassessment and resolution

Reassessed against the implementation and design contract on 2026-08-08:

Finding Assessment Resolution
1 Valid packaging bug Ignore numbered Cargo-target duplicates and CLAUDE.md; ignore generated vendor/config trees; remove numbered Makevars artifacts.
2 Valid metadata bug Bound strings at real encoded-byte boundaries and derive truncated from the actual bounded result.
3 Correctly withdrawn No implementation change.
4 Valid format inconsistency Use u32 for stored length in both block header and directory, reserve the directory’s remaining four bytes, and reject lengths outside the wire/64 MiB limit.
5 Valid missing invariant Treat the header field as the maximum decoded block size and reject any indexed block that exceeds it.
6 Valid schema bug Emit synopsis_error unconditionally as FALSE or TRUE.
7 Valid durability distinction Keep the fast non-syncing default and document that visibility-atomic rename is not crash durability.
8 Valid replacement bug Copy existing destination permissions to the completed temporary file before replacement.
9 Valid platform limitation Document the non-atomic backup/rollback fallback and its recoverable stranded-backup risk.
10 Valid performance defect Validate and read blocks directly into the final R raw vector, removing the per-block buffer, redundant seek, and Rust-to-R payload copy.
11 Valid coverage gap Retain the added pure-Rust empty-payload round-trip test.
12 Valid CRAN/documentation gap Add executable examples to every exported operation.
13 Valid minor cleanup Align the internal Cargo development version and add a print.rdz_info() method.

The Phase 1 readiness warnings were also accepted. Native eligibility and writing now share one boundary call so a supported root is traversed once, and executable Rust models plus byte-layout tests back the documented object and attribute directory entries. Nonzero object/attribute tables remain rejected until Phase 1 defines their semantic validation.

Post-fix verification:

Check Result
cargo fmt --check --manifest-path src/rust/Cargo.toml pass
cargo test --manifest-path src/rust/Cargo.toml 16/16 pass
Rscript -e 'testthat::test_local(reporter = "summary")' all four suites pass
R CMD build --no-manual 592 KB, 52-entry archive with no excluded build trees or guidance symlink
R CMD check --no-manual with the required Rust 1.88 toolchain Status: OK

A focused 100,000-element/row warm-cache read run also confirmed the direct-read path is operational. Its medians are recorded in current-state.md; it is a regression measurement, not a competitive native-codec claim.

Regression tests for findings 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, and 8, plus the missing coverage identified in finding 11, are in tests/testthat/test-review-findings.R, src/rust/src/container/writer.rs, and src/rust/src/container/reader.rs.

Gate assessment

Phase 0B’s exit criteria are met. The benchmark contract is reproducible, the three codec modes are testable, the native frame writes and validates bounded raw blocks through direct Rust IO (including the native-codec-ID test in reader.rs), and adding logical records will not force a redesign of codec identification, trailer discovery, or directory bounds.

test-correctness.R is genuinely broad — closures, environments, cycles, shared references, S4, bytecode, and CE_BYTES encodings. The Rust is defensively written throughout: checked arithmetic, try_reserve, canonical span validation, and no unwrap at the R boundary.

Two items are worth resolving before Phase 1 rather than during it; see Phase 1 readiness.

Confirmed bugs

1. .Rbuildignore gap ships 62 MB of Cargo artifacts

.Rbuildignore:11 has ^src/rust/target$, which is anchored and does not match src/rust/target 2/ — the macOS duplicate directory present in the working tree.

Verified: R CMD build produces a 21 MB tarball containing 385 entries under src/rust/target 2/, along with many storing paths of more than 100 bytes is not portable tar warnings.

^src/Makevars [0-9]+$ was already added for exactly this class of macOS duplicate; the rust target case was missed. Separately, CLAUDE.md ships as a dereferenced 9.7 KB regular file, because .Rbuildignore covers ^AGENTS\.md$ but not the symlink pointing at it.

Fix

  • Add ^src/rust/target( [0-9]+)?$ and ^CLAUDE\.md$ to .Rbuildignore.
  • Add a [0-9]* duplicate pattern to src/.gitignore.
  • Delete the stray src/rust/target 2/ and src/Makevars 2|3|4 from the tree.

2. rdz_info() reports truncated names while claiming truncated = FALSE

R/serialize.R:143 and R/serialize.R:157 compute the truncation flag from a byte threshold (> 256), but bound_rdz_strings() truncates to bytes %/% 4 = 64 code points. Any ASCII name between 65 and 256 characters is silently cut and then reported as complete.

Verified: a 70-character attribute name is returned as 64 characters with truncated = FALSE; a 100-character class name behaves the same way. The existing test in test-public-api.R uses 1000-character names, which clear the byte threshold and hide the window.

Because the synopsis’s entire contract in metadata-access.md is to label what it does not know, this is the worst possible place for a false negative.

Fix: derive the flag from the actual result — compare the bounded value against the original with identical() — instead of maintaining a parallel heuristic that can disagree with the bounding function.

3. WITHDRAWN — names(attributes(x)) does not materialize attribute values

Originally raised as a write-path allocation problem at R/serialize.R:153, on the theory that attributes() builds every attribute value and expands a data frame’s compact row names. That was a measurement error and the finding does not stand.

The original evidence was object.size(attributes(df)$row.names) reporting 19.1 MB for a 5-million-row frame. object.size() reports the notional materialized size of an ALTREP compact sequence, not the memory actually allocated. Measured properly:

bench::bench_memory(a <- attributes(data.frame(x = 1:5e6)))$mem_alloc  # 0 bytes
.Internal(inspect(a$row.names))  # INTSXP ... 1 : 5000000 (compact)

Compact row names come back as an ALTREP compact sequence, and every other attribute value is shared by pointer rather than copied — identical() on the address confirms it for a 5-million-element names attribute. attributes() allocates only a short list of pointers plus the character vector of names, so the cost is O(number of attributes) and does not scale with object size.

Recorded here rather than deleted so the question is not reopened.

Format decisions cheaper to settle now than after Phase 1

4. Block-header stored length is u32; the directory entry’s is u64

Compare container-format.md:83 with container-format.md:129; the two are checked against each other at reader.rs:291.

Harmless under MAX_BLOCK_SIZE = 64 MiB, but once compression makes stored_len != decoded_len the asymmetry becomes real. Pick one width.

Related: writer.rs:146 performs an unchecked entry.stored_len as u32 truncating cast, on the shared write_container path that Phase 1 will reuse.

5. The header’s nominal block size is bounds-checked but never cross-validated

reader.rs:103 bounds the field, but nothing validates it against the actual blocks — yet rdz_info()$block_size reports it to the user as fact. Either validate it (all blocks but the last must equal it) or document it as informational.

6. synopsis_error exists only on the failure path

Compare R/serialize.R:127 with R/serialize.R:161. container-format.md presents synopsis_error as the flag consumers check, but on the success path the field is absent — NULL rather than FALSE — and the two lists differ in length. Emit it unconditionally so the synopsis has a stable schema.

IO semantics

7. “Atomic” here means crash-visible, not crash-durable

writer.rs:91 calls file.flush(), which is a no-op for std::fs::File, and there is no sync_all() before the rename in atomic_file.rs:62. A crash can therefore leave a renamed but unflushed file.

This is a defensible tradeoff that most serializers make, but a package whose pitch is integrity should state it explicitly rather than let flush() imply otherwise. Consider an opt-in sync mode.

8. Replacement widens file permissions

The temporary file is created at the default mode and umask (atomic_file.rs:33) and then renamed over the destination, so replacing a 0600 .rdz file yields a 0644 one. saveRDS preserves the existing mode.

9. The cross-device / sharing-violation fallback in commit() is not atomic

In the fallback branch the destination does not exist between the two renames, and a crash there strands a .name-rdz-N.backup file. Worth documenting as a known limitation of the non-rename(2) path.

Performance headroom on the path being measured

10. The read path copies the payload three times

reader.rs:57-65 allocates and zero-fills a per-block Vec, reads into it, then extend_from_slice into payload. lib.rs:36 then copies that buffer into a fresh R raw vector, and unserialize() reads it again.

Two of the three are removable:

  1. Read directly into payload’s tail — resize then read_exact(&mut payload[start..]), and CRC that subslice.
  2. Better, allocate OwnedRawSexp::new(len) up front and read blocks into as_mut_slice(). Both APIs are confirmed present in savvy 0.10.2.

current-state.md names “a raw-buffer allocation, file pass, and mandatory CRC scan” as the reason RDZ loses to uncompressed base R on simple atomic payloads. This is the cheapest part of that to reclaim, and it is independent of the streaming callback bridge deferred to Phase 8.

Also: the seek at reader.rs:56 is redundant, because validate_block_header leaves the cursor exactly at payload_offset.

Coverage gaps

11. The empty-payload branch is unreachable from R and untested in Rust

writer.rs:76-78. serialize() never returns zero bytes, so R cannot reach this path, and no Rust test passes an empty slice. Tracing it by hand shows it does round-trip correctly, but the reader’s block_count == 0 rejection and its zero-length block handling go unexercised — and a native codec writing an empty vector will be the first thing to hit them.

12. No \examples{} in any exported function

None of write_rdz, read_rdz, or rdz_info has an examples block, so R CMD check runs no example code at all. CRAN will also require them.

13. Minor

  • src/rust/Cargo.toml declares version = "0.1.0" while DESCRIPTION declares 0.0.0.9000.
  • class(info) <- "rdz_info" is set in R/serialize.R:95 with no corresponding print method.

Phase 1 readiness

Two structural items are better resolved before the logical vertical slice than during it.

The eligibility interface will bake in a double traversal. rdz_select_codec() computes native eligibility and discards it (r_adapter.rs:56), returning only a codec name. A native write will therefore traverse the SEXP twice — once to decide, once to encode. Fusing them into a single Rust call that returns either an encoded result or the distinguished unsupported-native outcome avoids committing to the double traversal in the interface shape.

The object and attribute directory entries exist only as prose. They are described in container-format.md but have no Rust structs, and the reader hard-rejects nonzero counts (reader.rs:197). “Reserved” currently means “documented”. Phase 1 is the first real test of whether the 48-byte object entry and 32-byte attribute entry are the right shape.
